column4: In the early 20th century, Kunffy portrayed local rural Romani people. He depicted them as powerful, unbroken counter-images to the “respectable Hungarian society.”
Stylized clothing, long hair, serious expressions; representation as strong, earthy “types.” No threat, but respectful portrayal. Still, ethnographic stereotyping is present.
Visual Culture, Ethnographic Representation, Stereotype Analysis
Stereotyping as ethnographic type without individual biography; respectful yet distanced. Not a discriminatory framing, but generalization remains.
How do ethnographic-stereotypical representations of Roma affect contemporary memory?
